atoms.a:
Joseph is walking around the supermarket.
He fills his basket with a loaf of bread weighing 400g, a bag of apples weighing 1.2kg and a bottle of milk that weighs 2.3kg. The basket itself weighs 210g when empty.

How much does the basket weigh when Joseph’s items are in it?
atoms.sound: Joseph is walking around the supermarket. He fills his basket with a loaf of bread weighing 400 grams, a bag of apples weighing 1.2 kilograms and a bottle of milk that weighs 2.3 kilograms. The basket itself weighs 210g when empty. atoms.a: How much will the basket weigh when Joseph swaps his loaf of bread for a packet of tortillas weighing 537 g?

atoms.sound: His basket will now weigh 4.247 kilograms.

atoms.a:
Jess is reorganising the kitchen cupboards. The first cupboard can hold up to 45 kg. Jess puts in 37.23 kg worth of stuff.

How much more can Jess put in the cupboard?

atoms.b: Jess can add <mat><gap>7.77</gap></mat>kg worth of stuff to the cupboard.

atoms.a: Jess puts some jars weighing 2.47 kg in the cupboard. How much more can she put in the cupboard now?

atoms.b: Jess can put <mat><gap>5.3 5.30</gap></mat> kg more in the cupboard.

atoms.a:
Jess’s other cupboard can only hold 12 kg.
Jess puts in a pot weighing 983 g, some glasses weighing 312 g, her tupperware boxes weighing 693 g and a few frying pans, which weigh 1435 g.

How much more can Jess put in the cupboard? First add up how much her items weigh.
Now subtract the weight of the items from the weight limit of her cupboard.

hint.text: Don’t forget to convert to kilograms!

atoms.b: Jess can put another <mat><gap>8.577</gap></mat> kg in the cupboard.
